## Today's Plan

-   Review Git

-   10 tips I find helpful to know

-   Live demo: doing all of this with buttons in Positron

## By the end of today, you will (probably) know how to:

- Do the everyday git workflow from Positron's Git pane
- How to undo things in Git
- How to read git history

## Tip 1: `git status` is your best friend

- Run it constantly! It tells you what's changed, what's staged, and what's untracked
- When in doubt, run `git status` first.

## Tip 2: Git Workflow

1. Pull
2. Create/switch branch
3. Make your changes
4. Commit
5. Push

## Tip 3: Don't forget to use multiple branches

- Once you've used a branch and made a commit, *delete* it

## Tip 4: How to read git history

- git log in the terminal
- Gives entire history of commits in the repository
- git log --oneline

## Tip 5: Have good commit descriptions

- Better able to read git log + collaborate

## Tip 6: Always review before commiting

- See exactly what you changed with git status or git diff

## Tip 7: Be intentional with commits

- You don't need to commit every file
- Option to commit gitignore, you don't need to

## Tip 8: Changing themes

- You can change your theme 

## Tip 9: You can always re-add a repository to your computer

- I've found that if my local git is tweaking, just recopy it from github

## Tip 10: Git can undo things

- Undo an unstaged file
- Undo a staged file
- Undo/ammend a commit
- https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Basics-Undoing-Things

## Key Takeaways

1. Check `git status` and `git diff` before every commit
2. Write clear commit messages and use branches
3. Git can undo most mistakes, so don't panic
